title: Uldaman
body: Uldaman lies buried beneath the northern Badlands, a vault of the titans far older than any dwarven hold, cut from the living rock on a scale no mortal mason ever attempted. The dwarves of Ironforge broke into it looking for the origins of their people, and lost it when the Stonevault troggs boiled up from the depths. The Shadowforge clan of the Dark Iron dwarves digs behind barricades of its own, and deeper in the vault keeps guardians of living stone.

parts.body: The Shadowforge dig for strange stones that, treated rightly, are stable sources of power. They learned the secret from a goblin they took to Angor Fortress, then threw him out.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Uldaman (pre-Cataclysm official description: an ancient titan vault buried deep within the earth; dwarven digs penetrated it and released the troggs; Dark Iron incursions; guardians of living stone); its disc and creation lore is left out

parts.body: Hammertoe Grez, their prisoner, begs for the amulet Magregan Deepshadow took from him, before it leads the Shadowforge to what they are looking for.

title: The Hall of the Keepers
body: Past the gate of the vault proper opens its first great hall, the Hall of the Keepers, and the Stonevault troggs hold it in force, their oracles raising shields of lightning and spouts of lava. Side digs lead off it, and in one corner, where the troggs pay them no mind, lie the remains of a paladin, left where he fell.

parts.body: The paladin carried a necklace made by Talvash del Kissel of Ironforge. His journal tells where its three gems went: the Shadowforge, the troggs and their king Grimlok each took one.

title: The Halls of Living Stone
body: Beyond the halls the troggs hold, the vault is kept by earthen, figures of living stone that do not speak and do not let anyone pass. They guard the Temple Hall and, further east, the grander Hall of the Crafters, where four stone keepers stand as still as statues around an altar before a closed temple door.

parts.body: In a side cave crawling with scorpids hides Annora, an enchanter, who had begun to think she would have to hide out forever. What brought her so deep she does not say.

title: Ironaya
body: Ironaya is a guardian of Uldaman, a towering figure of iron sealed in the Chamber of Khaz'mul behind a great carved seal that only the right key will open. When the way is opened she strides out with a warning: none may steal the secrets of the Makers.

parts.body: Baelog of the Explorers' League was sure the chamber existed and knew how to open it. If Ironforge ever takes Uldaman back, the League means its secrets to be theirs.

title: Archaedas
body: Archaedas, the Ancient Stone Watcher, sits in Khaz'goroth's Seat, the great chamber beneath the Hall of the Crafters, a giant of living stone among rows of stone dwarves as still as he is. Behind him the door of the Ancient Vault stays shut, and calling upon the altar before him wakes him to the wrath of the Makers. Whatever lies in the vault, he is its last guard.

title: The Discs of Norgannon
body: Beyond Archaedas lies the Ancient Vault, and at its heart four huge platinum discs adorned with sigils of no known origin. At a touch the image of a great stone watcher springs up beside them, the Lore Keeper of Norgannon. The Creators' making of the earthen is recorded here, it says, and it waits to be asked.

parts.body: The titans made the earthen from the stone of Azeroth to shape its deep places. Under strain their making came undone in two ways: the troggs, who lost their minds, and the dwarves, who turned to flesh.
sources: quest 2278 description (four huge platinum discs; sigils of unknown origin; your hand tingles; the visage of a large stone watcher springs forth; Salutations, I am a keeper of knowledge; stored here for this world in the Discs of Norgannon)

parts.body: The Creators judged the dwarf an acceptable variant, worthy of genesis in its own right. It is the proof the Explorers' League has been digging for.
